transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Thank you, doctor. Honestly, I'm here because I find myself going out of my way to avoid absolutely anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin. It's gotten to the point where I'm cutting out important parts of my own life just to keep from remembering.
Can you tell me more about what specifically happens when you're reminded of what happened to your cousin, do you experience any distressing thoughts, feelings, or physical sensations?

When I'm reminded, I suddenly see my cousin's body in the coffin or hear my aunt describing the shooting like a horrible clip playing in my head, and my chest tightens so much that I just freeze. I'm immediately flooded with this heavy dread and guilt, feeling like I somehow failed him by not getting him out of Guatemala sooner.
How long have you been experiencing these intrusive thoughts and images of your cousin's death, and have they been present every day since it happened?

These intrusive images have been happening steadily since I came back from Guatemala after his funeral, which was a little over a year ago—about 14 months now. They happen almost every day, popping up out of nowhere while I'm at my desk working or just cooking dinner.

Do you ever feel compelled to perform specific rituals or repetitive behaviors in an attempt to reduce your distress or prevent something bad from happening, or are your actions mainly focused on avoiding reminders of your cousin's death?

No, I don't have any rituals or repetitive behaviors like that. My actions are entirely focused on avoiding reminders of his death, so I stay off buses, avoid Spanish news, and have muted family group chats and Guatemalan community events. I do this because I am absolutely terrified that if I hear one more story or see one more image, I’ll completely fall apart.
Do you often find yourself on edge, having difficulty sleeping, or easily startled since your cousin's death, and if so, how have these symptoms affected your daily life?

Yes, I'm constantly on edge and lie in bed exhausted but wired, waking up from vivid dreams about buses and feeling completely unrefreshed. I also jump out of my skin at sudden noises or if someone walks up behind me at work, and it takes a long time to calm down. This constant exhaustion has caused my work performance to slip with missed deadlines, and I've pulled back from my family because I just have no energy left.

You've mentioned avoiding reminders and having intrusive thoughts, but can you tell me if these thoughts are always about your cousin's death or if they sometimes involve fears of harm coming to yourself or others in a way that doesn't directly relate to your cousin's passing?

Yes, the intrusive thoughts and mental images are always directly related to my cousin's death, like suddenly seeing him in his coffin or hearing my aunt describe the shooting. I don't have unrelated fears of harm coming to myself or other people, though I do carry a constant, heavy sense of dread and guilt specifically tied to feeling like I failed him.
Can you elaborate on what specifically makes you feel like you failed your cousin, is it something you did or didn't do before or after his death that contributes to this overwhelming sense of guilt?

I feel a deep sense of guilt because I feel like I failed him by not being there when it happened, or by not helping him get out of Guatemala sooner. This heavy feeling of dread sits underneath everything I do now, coloring even my ordinary days so they all feel heavy and slightly wrong. It's just this constant weight that I can't seem to shake.
Do you believe that if you had acted differently, your cousin's death could have been prevented, and is this belief what drives your feeling of having failed him?

Yes, I really believe that. I feel like if I had just helped him get out of Guatemala sooner, he would still be alive today. That deep conviction that I should have done something to prevent it is exactly what drives this constant guilt and makes every day feel so heavy.
Do you think that your guilt and belief about failing your cousin are realistic, or do you think they might be an exaggerated or distorted way of thinking about what happened?

Intellectually, I know it might be unrealistic or distorted since I live in New York and couldn't control an armed robbery in Guatemala. But emotionally, the guilt feels incredibly real and heavy, and I constantly feel like I failed him by not getting him out of the country sooner. It just colors everything I do and makes every day feel wrong.

Do you often find yourself excessively replaying the events leading up to your cousin's death, thinking about what you could have done differently to change the outcome, and if so, how does this replaying affect your daily functioning and relationships?

Yes, I constantly replay those thoughts alongside my aunt's description of the shooting, which often makes me freeze up. This has caused me to miss deadlines and avoid collaborative meetings at work, which has hurt my performance reviews. I've also pulled back so much from family visits and community events that my husband and relatives are constantly asking why I'm never around anymore.
